Annual awards recognize customers turning cyber resilience into a competitive advantage

DALLAS, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced the recipients of the 2026 TrendAI™ Cybersecurity Excellence Awards. The awards celebrate organizations worldwide for their leadership, innovation, and excellence in cybersecurity.

The winners across the five categories are listed below.

Innovator recognizes organizations introducing new ideas, technologies, or approaches that meaningfully advance cybersecurity

Winners: Sun Chemical; Taiwan Mobile; MITSUI SUMITOMO INSURANCE Agency Service; Qassim University

Visionary honors organizations that are transforming a bold cybersecurity vision into measurable progress

Winners: Pegasystems; SoftBank

Cyber Defender celebrates those demonstrating an exceptional commitment to protecting people, operations, and digital environments

Winners: Keller ISD; Ministry of Environment, Water, and Agriculture (MEWA); Servico de Salud de las Baleras (IBSalut)

Ambassador distinguishes leaders championing stronger cybersecurity practices across their industries and communities

Winners: Cape Cod Healthcare; Anglicare Victoria; Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board

AI Trailblazer highlights an individual advancing the responsible and effective use of AI in cybersecurity

Winners: Dole Food Company; Pets at Home; International SOS Assistance UK Limited; Rural Servicios Informáticos

Cybersecurity is no longer only about preventing compromise. Organizations that manage it well strengthen customer trust, enable digital transformation, and gain a competitive edge. The 2026 award recipients demonstrate what that looks like in practice.

Rachel Jin, CEO of TrendAI™: "This year's Cybersecurity Excellence Awards represent the next generation of security-first leaders who understand that cyber resilience is not a compliance checkbox, but a competitive advantage. These customers have transformed how they approach risk, turning threat intelligence into innovation, and weaving security into the fabric of business strategy. That's what true excellence looks like."

What the award winners have to say:

Florian Zeeb, Director of Global Information Security, Dole Food Group: "Security needs a seat at the table when AI is adopted, not a review at the end. That is how we make sure AI is used securely and ethically. It only works with the support of management and the teams, and we had both. This recognition is theirs as much as mine. Nobody had all the answers. We learned together with our partners, and we keep learning."

Takashi Hara, Manager, SoftBank: "We are deeply honored to receive the Visionary Award. At SoftBank, we are committed to advancing cybersecurity as a critical foundation for driving social and industrial transformation through cutting-edge technologies, including AI. We understand this recognition reflects our efforts not only to address evolving cyber threats, but also to harness AI safely and responsibly to create new value. Going forward, we will continue to tackle emerging security risks associated with the growing adoption of AI and strengthen our governance frameworks. At the same time, we will advance AI-driven threat detection and analysis, as well as the sophistication of our security operations, with the goal of further enhancing our overall cybersecurity posture."

Liviu Groza, Director Information Security, Cape Cod Healthcare: "This Excellence Award is a reflection on the value Cape Cod Healthcare places on cybersecurity and on TrendAI's ability to meet the demands of operating seemlesly in a space as diverse and sensitive as healthcare. In an increasingly hostile and difficult threat environment, we are able to support the delicate act of healing without undue burden, thanks to organizational backing at all levels and TrendAI's feature rich product suite."

TrendAI™ runs NVIDIA Nemotron open models entirely inside customer-controlled infrastructure, delivering AI-driven threat detection and policy-based response without security data ever leaving the sovereign boundary.

DALLAS, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today announced it is bringing NVIDIA Nemotron™ open models into TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC), building on its collaboration with NVIDIA. The integration brings AI-assisted security operations into customer-controlled environments, extending capabilities such as guided investigation, security reasoning, and agentic SIEM to organizations with sovereignty, data residency and operational control.

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) is available today, enabling organizations to deploy TrendAI Vision One™ in customer-controlled private cloud, sovereign cloud and on-premises environments. The Nemotron integration extends AI-assisted security operations into these environments while maintaining customer control over security data and deployment.

Why Open Models Matter for SovereigntyHighly regulated organizations need AI-driven security that fits their data-control requirements. Nemotron open models can support these requirements by bringing the model to the data rather than the data to the model. Customers decide where the model runs, which version is deployed, and who can access it, running AI-powered security operations on NVIDIA accelerated computing in their own data centers, sovereign clouds, and restricted-connectivity environments. TrendAI™ collaboration with NVIDIA on OpenShell provides an additional level of security for agents, ensuring organizations have control and visibility of agentic activities.

Who Controls the Intelligence Acting on Your Data?"Sovereignty extends beyond where data resides. Enterprises also need control over where the intelligence acting on that data operates, and how it is governed." says Rachel Jin, CEO, TrendAI™. "Organizations shouldn't have to give up the operational benefits of AI because their security data and operations need to remain within a customer-controlled environment. Our work is about bringing AI-powered security operations to the environments our customers choose to control."

"Open models give organizations the transparency and control to run on their own terms, which is critical for sovereign environments," said John Fanelli, Vice President, Enterprise Software at NVIDIA. "TrendAI's integration of NVIDIA Nemotron models enables enterprises to put their most sensitive data to work, without it ever leaving their control."

Customer Perspective: Sovereignty Without CompromiseTITECH, which delivers sovereign security operations to customers in Oman, is working with TrendAI™ as a design partner on the Nemotron integration ahead of general availability.

"TrendAI Vision One for Sovereign and Private Cloud has provided our local customers in Oman with a trusted foundation for keeping security operations under customer control while complying with country data residency regulations," says TITECH CEO, Mohammed Hassan. "Nemotron-powered capabilities will let us offer advanced threat analysis and AI-assisted security operations to our customers while maintaining data sovereignty and operational control."

The integration supports AI-assisted threat analysis, policy-based response, and guided security operations within customer-controlled environments. These capabilities help organizations improve security operations with AI while maintaining control over where security data and AI processing reside.

Customer Outcome: Security and control from the start"As enterprises apply AI to real-world deployment, security and control must be embedded into the infrastructure from day one," says Business Manager of Security at Bechtle AG, Mathias Schick. "Our customers want to harness the full potential of AI without compromising data sovereignty, security, or operational control. Integrating AI-powered security into sovereign and private-cloud environments is an important step toward enabling secure AI adoption at scale, particularly for organizations with stringent security and compliance requirements."

TrendAI Vision One™ for Sovereign and Private Cloud (SPC) with NVIDIA Nemotron integration supports:

Customer-controlled AI: NVIDIA Nemotron open models deployed and run on customer-controlled infrastructure, with no dependency on external inference services

AI-assisted threat analysis: Reasoning across security signals to identify complex threat patterns, attack chains, and AI-native attack paths

Policy-based threat response: Supporting protective actions through organization-defined policies and security-team controls

Guided security operations: Helping security teams investigate threats and prioritize response activities

Agentic SIEM capabilities: Correlating telemetry and assisting with security reasoning while maintaining team oversight

Full Text:
Ethical hackers discovered 98 unique zero-day vulnerabilities at the three-day event, advancing the techniques defenders use to find and fix flaws at AI speed

CORK, Ireland, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader from Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today celebrated the efforts of the global security research community at Pwn2Own Ireland by awarding a total of $1,262,000 in prizes. Contestants discovered and disclosed 98 unique zero-day vulnerabilities across categories including: mobile phones; smart home devices; wellness; printers; messaging; AI infrastructure; and AI coding agents.

Dustin Childs, Head of Threat Awareness at TrendAI's Zero Day Initiative: "The vulnerabilities discovered at Pwn2Own are sent to vendors so they can patch them quickly. Having visibility into these vulnerabilities also helps protect TrendAI customers via virtual patching. The lasting value of an event like this is what defenders learn. Every exploit chain demonstrated on stage teaches us something new about how modern systems break, and those lessons go directly into how we train our own research capability to discover, validate and remediate the next one faster. As AI tools and infrastructure continue to become central to business functions, staying ahead of vulnerabilities will be as critical as ever."

The devices on stage at Pwn2Own are deliberately familiar—phones, printers, smart home hubs, wearables—and that familiarity is the point. Watching a researcher chain several flaws together to take over a consumer phone makes visible a process that usually happens out of sight. It is the same process, and often the same class of flaw, that applies to the enterprise-grade systems behind global ecommerce, banking, critical infrastructure and healthcare.

The disclosures made through TrendAI™ ZDI at Pwn2Own and year-round allow vendors to quickly understand and fix vulnerabilities before cybercriminals exploit them, ultimately benefiting organizations and end users of the impacted software or hardware. TrendAI™ research has shown that vendors are increasingly neglecting to patch software vulnerabilities that are disclosed to them. Through the TrendAI™ ZDI coordinated disclosure process, TrendAI Vision One™ customers are protected an average of 115 days ahead of the rest of the industry.

Caroline Kiel, CEO, PingUs: "Watching live zero-day exploits demonstrated on stage was exciting. It was encouraging to see the vendors be onsite to encourage the researcher community to poke holes in their products. Seeing how Pwn2Own turns fresh vulnerability research into immediate protection proves how deeply committed TrendAI is to securing products across the entire ecosystem."

Highlights from the event included:

Ikotas Labs, Inc. earned the title, Master of Pwn and $300,000, after it chained multiple issues together to successfully exploit the Google Pixel 10 at the very end of the three-day competition. Ikotas Labs, Inc. is the first-ever Japanese team to claim the Master of Pwn title.

Xint, which placed second in the competition, earned $150,000 by successfully demonstrating a remote exploit of the Google Pixel 10 through a single bug collision.

Interrupt Labs earned $5,000 after it successfully took over the Lexmark CX532adwe printer and played DOOM on its screen.

The next Pwn2Own competition is expected in early 2027. For more details, please visit: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/blog

Title: TrendAI™ Research Reinforces Japan's Urgent Cybersecurity Warning as Incidents Surge in 2026
Context: " TrendAI™ Forward-Looking Threat Research data shows Japan recorded more publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of 2026 than in all of 2025
Full Text:
Japan-headquartered cybersecurity leader shares threat intelligence and practical guidance as AI accelerates the global threat landscape.

DALLAS, Oct. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrendAI™, the global AI security leader and enterprise business unit of Trend Micro Incorporated (TYO: 4704; TSE: 4704), today issued a threat advisory for organizations in Japan after Masaaki Taira, who chairs the Liberal Democratic Party's National Cybersecurity Strategy Headquarters, said that "cyberspace is in a state of emergency." TrendAI™ Forward-Looking Threat Research data shows Japan recorded more publicly disclosed cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of 2026 than in all of 2025. September alone saw 86 incidents, up about 18% from August and 37% from July.

The party's headquarters met on Oct. 9 in response to a series of cyberattacks on Japanese businesses and called on the government to strengthen public-private cooperation. Breaches at retailers, financial services firms, a car-sharing service and a rail operator have exposed data of millions of customers. The government's National Cybersecurity Office has sent guidance to ministries, local governments and private companies on keeping security protection up to date, using strong passwords and tightening security across supply chains.

The TrendAI™ Incident Response team has also seen a rise in incidents in Japan. In recent engagements, attackers exploited known vulnerabilities in public-facing applications to plant web shells on web servers, giving them a foothold from which they may attempt privilege escalation, lateral movement or access to connected databases. Japanese-language analysis of these cases from TrendAI™, along with hardening guidance, is available here.

"Cyberattacks are increasing globally, and so are the breaches and data leaks as a result. While AI might not be directly involved, its ability to help the attackers find targets and automate their operations makes cyberattacks scalable. Organizations need to shrink their cyber exposure and close the vulnerabilities in order to lower the odds of being victimized," said Ryan Flores, Co-lead, Forward-Looking Threat Research, TrendAI™.

AI is lowering the cost of attacks. TrendAI™ has not established a connection between the recent incidents in Japan and the use of AI by attackers. However, AI does let attackers accelerate reconnaissance, analyze vulnerabilities and produce convincing phishing in languages they do not speak. This weakens protections that languages, such as Japanese, once offered against foreign attackers. Automation also makes smaller organizations, including suppliers, more attractive targets given the increased return on investment for cybercriminals.

"While organizations around the world learn to work with their AI budgets, it's important to remember that AI has zero cost for cybercriminals," said Robert McArdle, Director, Forward-Looking Threat Research, TrendAI™. "There's already a robust economy for stolen accounts, APIs, and tokens, and this is driving the increasingly automated and agentic cybercrime campaigns we see today. The current surge in Japan should not be interpreted as a peak in criminal activity, it should be seen as the new baseline of attacks that will only increase in volume, speed, and relentlessness."

To harden protections, TrendAI™ recommends:

Patch internet-facing systems first. Keep an accurate inventory of public web servers, applications and cloud services, apply security updates promptly, prioritize vulnerabilities known to be actively exploited, and use virtual patching to cover the gap while fixes are tested and deployed.

Harden web servers. Restrict write access to application code, isolate file-upload directories, prevent uploaded content from running as scripts, and monitor for unauthorized changes to application files and configurations.

Watch database access. Monitor sensitive database operations and abnormal access patterns; run applications with minimum-privilege database accounts.

Check suppliers. Ask hosting and cloud providers how they would notify you of an incident, review which third parties hold customer data, and confirm critical services can recover independently of a single provider.

Strengthen identity verification. Review processes that rely solely on uploaded photographs of identity documents and adopt chip-based or other stronger verification consistent with regulatory guidance.

Bring AI usage into scope. Identify AI applications, models, and agents used across the organization, assess their provenance and reputation, review their access to sensitive data and internal systems, and apply appropriate security controls and approval processes.

TrendAI™ threat researchers and incident responders are tracking the activity behind the current wave of incidents in Japan and will publish further findings as the analysis continues. Organizations that want to discuss their exposure can contact their TrendAI™ account team.

In addition, the TrendAI Vision One™ platform is purpose-built to help organizations address their expanding AI security risks due to shadow AI, sensitive data submitted to external services, or AI agents connected to internal systems with excessive permissions. Vision One operates on a unified model of visibility, observability, actionability, and governance, spanning endpoints, cloud, identity, data, and AI, giving security practitioners the tools to anticipate and stop threats across their attack surface before they impact the business. To help organizations further identify and reduce AI risk, TrendAI is introducing new capabilities to its Vision One AI security suite in December 2026, including AI Gateway and AI Risk Insights solutions with digital asset reputation scoring. With the addition of these new controls in Vision One, organizations can holistically achieve:
